notes: Configurations are full-model-v6 (with_skill) vs the pre-edit full-model-v5 snapshot (old_skill) — an A/B of the edit, not a skill-vs-no-skill test.
eval-1 is the sharpest discriminator: v6 built the 1 Pager + NTM PE pair the finished workbooks actually carry (5/5); v5 built a DCF (1/5), which no finished workbook contains.

eval-0 anchor assertion is convention-neutral by design: a hardcode build must match values, a link build must target the same VAActuals rows the user's finished Mini Model uses. v6 aligned 3/3 on rows; v5's hardcodes matched 8/15 values (its misses trace to a 2022 start year vs the ground truth's 2021), so v5's arithmetic was largely right and its failure is convention, not accuracy.
Assertion 'no pre-existing tab modified / zero error cells' passes in every run — non-discriminating, keep only as a regression guard.
Cost of the edit: v6 averaged ~245k tokens vs v5 ~263k, and ~34 min vs ~38 min per run — the restructured skill was slightly cheaper and faster despite building more tabs in eval-1 (two tabs vs one).
Single run per cell (no repeats), so treat per-eval numbers as directional; the eval-1 and eval-2 gaps are structural (which tabs/engines get built) rather than noise-sensitive.

Offline caveat: v6's VA-linked Mini Model renders #NAME? until opened with the Visible Alpha add-in (289 such cells), because VAActuals itself is live _xll.VAData. That matches the user's own finished workbooks, but it does mean a v6 deliverable looks empty until it reaches the analyst's desktop.
